title: Blood of Christ
definition: The blood of Christ refers to His sacrificial death by which He secures forgiveness, cleansing, redemption, and peace with God.
summary: The blood of Christ cleanses sinners and secures redemption.
christFocus: Jesus shed His blood as the mediator of the new covenant and the Lamb of God who takes away sin.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The blood of Christ points to His life poured out in sacrificial death. Scripture connects His blood with redemption, cleansing, forgiveness, covenant, peace, and victory.

This language is not empty symbolism. It shows that sin required a true atoning sacrifice, and Christ willingly gave Himself.

Through His blood, believers are brought near, cleansed from guilt, and purchased for God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often want forgiveness without sacrifice. The blood of Christ matters because it shows the cost of mercy and the certainty of cleansing.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest in the cleansing power of Christ's blood. Do not trust guilt, shame, or self-payment above what He has accomplished.
